## Conclusion

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve — Aurora kinase inhibitors at 0.88 is justified.** Final protocol vote (e9) is 3/4 for Aurora, agreeing with the conclusion, with high per-well similarities (0.82–0.88) for the three Aurora wells vs 0.57 for the single 10 µM DNA-damage outlier, and 9/10 neighbours Aurora (mean 0.78 vs 0.61). Phenotype discriminates from the runner-up: reproducible ~2× integrated DNA, frac_large_nucleus z=+70 to +107, and binucleate/bilobed enlarged nuclei with intact tubulin/actin (e2, e5, e7, e8) fit failed cytokinesis/polyploidy, not DNA-damage arrest; Eg5/microtubule classes are contradicted by negative frac_mitotic_like and preserved cytoskeleton. Acquisitions were discriminative — a replicate at dose 4 (1 µM, rep 2) and a bridging dose 5 (3 µM, rep 1) resolved the initial 1/1 split at e4 — so the key effect is not single-well. The negative dose-response rho is driven by the 10 µM drop-off and does not overturn the 1–3 µM replication. Budget is exhausted (0/4 left) and no further affordable well could change this.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ258** (PubChem CID [59396138](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/59396138))

Identity check: from the BBBC021 structure (the name is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (3/4). The Scientist's own call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The Aurora kinase inhibitor call was driven by an extreme and reproducible enlarged-nucleus signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+70.3 to +106.7 and nuc_area z=+38.0 to +46.4 at 1-3 uM (e2, e7, e8) with microscopist binucleate/bilobed enlarged nuclei and intact tubulin/actin (e5). The final atlas comparison at 3/4 NSC votes and 9/10 neighbours for Aurora at high similarity 0.82-0.88 correctly anchored the conclusion (e9).

The main misleading signals were the 10 uM well voting DNA damage at low similarity 0.57 (e3) and the negative dose-response rho=-0.63, p=0.37 for frac_large_nucleus and nuc_area (e10, e11). I treated these as high-dose drop-off with cell loss to 203 cells rather than a true inverse trend, since the 1 uM replicate and 3 uM bridge dose reproduced the Aurora phenotype and similarity.

The discriminative acquisition choices were the 1 uM replicate and 3 uM bridging well, which resolved the initial 1/2 split vote (e4) to a decisive 3/4 vote. This persistence of tetraploid/binucleate cells is consistent with literature on adaptation to genome doubling (PMID 27559130).

What was right:
- frac_large_nucleus z=+70.3 to +106.7 and nuc_area z=+38.0 to +46.4 with nuc_major_axis enlargement correctly identified polyploidy (e2, e7, e8)
- describe_phenotype binucleate/bilobed enlarged nuclei with lower density and preserved cytoskeleton correctly favored failed cytokinesis over DNA-damage arrest and excluded Eg5/microtubule classes (e5)
- compare_to_reference_atlas final 3/4 NSC votes and 9/10 neighbours for Aurora at 0.82-0.88 similarity correctly outweighed the single low-similarity 0.57 DNA-damage vote (e9)
- replicate 1 uM rep 2 and bridging 3 uM acquisitions confirmed reproducibility and resolved the early 1/2 split (e7, e8)

What was wrong or missed:
- dose_response rho=-0.63 p=0.37 for frac_large_nucleus and nuc_area was misleading; driven by the 10 uM cell-loss drop-off (203 cells), not a true inverse dose trend across 1-3 uM (e10, e11)
- early 1/2 NSC vote over-weighted DNA damage from the single high-dose well; that well matched DNA damage only at low similarity 0.57 versus 0.82-0.88 for Aurora wells (e3, e4)
- did not sample low doses 0.01-0.3 uM to define onset/EC50, leaving the lower end of the dose-response untested

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry with phospho-histone H3 staining plus live-cell imaging of mitosis and cytokinesis versus a reference Aurora inhibitor to confirm polyploidy from cytokinesis failure.
